sentences.text: CRL.P No. 5903 of 2024
THIS CRL.P IS FILED U/S.482 OF CR.P.C PRAYING TO a.

SET ASIDE THE ORDER OF TAKING COGNIZANCE DATED 21.07.2022 PASSED BY THE XXXIX ADDL.C.M.M., BENGALURU IN C.C.NO.23369/2022 FOR THE OFFENCE P/U/S 420 R/W 34 OF IPC BASED ON THE CHARGE SHEET FILED BY THE RESPONDENT NO.1/KORAMANGALA P.S.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE HEMANT CHANDANGOUDAR  ORAL ORDER
The petitioner/accused No.4, who is facing charges for offences punishable under Sections 420 and 34 of the IPC, is before this Court seeking relief.

2. The prosecution alleges that accused Nos.1 and 2 are the directors of Terrenum Homes India Pvt.
Ltd, a company engaged in real estate activities and property development in and around Bangalore.

It is alleged that accused Nos. 1 and 2 induced respondent No. 2 and other charge-sheet witnesses to purchase flats in an ongoing project, and in lieu of this, respondent No. 2 and the other witnesses deposited money with the company for the purchase of the flats.

Although the complainant was willing to purchase the flat by depositing the balance sale consideration amount, accused Nos. 1 and 2, as directors of the company, neither registered the sale deed nor returned the deposited amount.

The allegation against accused No. 4 is that, while working NC: 2025:KHC:10467 in the company's office, she collected the money and issued receipts to respondent No.2 and two other charge-sheet witnesses.
3.
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned counsel for respondent No.2, and the learned HCGP for the State.
4. It is admitted that the petitioner/accused No. 4 is not a director of the company that received the advance sale consideration from the complainant and the two other charge-sheet witnesses.

The responsibility to complete the project and register the sale deed rests with the company's directors,
not with the petitioner, who is an employee.

Mere receipt of money paid toward the advance sale Deepika vs State Of Karnataka on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120005360/
2 consideration and the issuance of receipts will not constitute an offence of cheating unless it is established that the petitioner, in collusion with the other accused, induced the complainant and the other charge-sheet witnesses to invest with an intention to deceive.

5. In the absence of the essential elements required to constitute the offences alleged against the petitioner, the continuation of the criminal proceedings would amount to an abuse of the process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. The criminal petition is allowed.
ii. The impugned proceedings in C.C.No.23369/2022 pending on the file of XXXIX ACMM, Bangalore NC: 2025:KHC:10467 insofar it relates to the petitioner/accused No.4 is hereby quashed.
iii. The trial court to proceed against other accused in accordance with law without being influenced by any observations made in this order.

Sd/-
(HEMANT CHANDANGOUDAR) JUDGE HDK CT: BHK Deepika vs State Of Karnataka on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120005360/
